findings.statement: A finite-setting rule with same-run throughput correction improves over the regularized source-family queue model on both reserved locations, but fails its improvement claim against the matched flexible control.
findings.applicability: Q4/Q5 within the same seven-location installation; six offered rates1,10,50,100,200,500Mbit/s. No unseen offered-rate extrapolation, hardware transfer, pure radio latency or intervention claim.
findings.limitations: Reference loses to RBF on Q5 and overall; no best-in-class or physical-law claim.
findings.falsification: Reference loses to RBF on Q5 and overall; no best-in-class or physical-law claim.
findings.prior_art: Source already establishes load-dependent empirical delay; offered-condition calibration and LAD are established methods.

findings.statement: The small development gain from a shared within-setting achieved-throughput slope does not survive both reserved locations.
findings.applicability: Within this installation and run-summary precision only.

findings.falsification: A0.5Mbps perturbation changes the frozen prediction by0.5895ms; adverse Q5 transfer is retained.
findings.prior_art: Same-run traffic and delay are mutually conditioned outcomes, not randomized predictors.

equation_or_program.expression: Ablation Lhat=m_a; unrestricted slope adds1.179 ms per Mbit/s at fixed offered rate.
